purpose: Positive-control diagnostic (operator 'try that next'): WHERE is there oracle-distinct headroom a learned verifier could capture? Computed from CACHED cross-domain pools (exp4305/exp4314); no generation.

metric_definitions.oracle_at_k: fraction of tasks where the correct answer is among the K candidates (selectable upper bound)
metric_definitions.sc_vote: fraction where the majority-vote (self-consistency) candidate is correct (baseline)
metric_definitions.headroom: oracle_at_k - sc_vote = selectable headroom a verifier could capture
metric_definitions.oracle_distinct: true if NO cheap executable oracle defines correctness (code/arc-exec/sudoku = circular = false)

per_domain.note: ONLY oracle-distinct domain with real headroom

no_headroom_corpora.MuSR: SC near-ceiling -> the entire PHASE D null streak (uPRM -0.110, LoRA-EBM/EBRM +0.080 CI-incl-0, process-reward -0.030, replay-memory -0.05) is a no-headroom artifact, not a method failure
no_headroom_corpora.math_csp_P0.1: strong classical baselines near-optimal (prior bounded nulls)

prior_fover_attempt_collapsed.result: cross-domain (held-out FoVer) verifier-select beat vote by +0.231 BUT label_ablation reproduced +0.231 identically -> label-independent artifact
prior_fover_attempt_collapsed.implication: FoVer headroom is REAL but UNCAPTURED; the cross-domain transfer was an artifact
